The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 08.04.2023 at about 4.30 pm., when the petitioner was pedestrian on the extreme left side of the Ring Road, near Yogeshwarnagar Cross, Bengaluru City in order to cross SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.2735/2023 the road in a direction of North to South, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KH-2564 came from Hebbal side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately, after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Bangalore Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru after first aid treatment he was referred to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 08.0.2023 to 14.04.2023 wherein after conservative treatment he was referred to Gopala Gowda Shanthaveri Memorial Hospital, Nazarbad medical Services Pvt. Ltd., Mysuru wherein the petitioner taken treatment as an inpatient from 14.04.2023 to 21.04.2023 and spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 08.04.2023 at about 4.30 pm., and the FIR at Ex.P1 in crime No.0080/2023 came to be registered on 10.04.2023 at around 15.30, at Hebbal Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.

Thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.11 against the rider of the alleged motor cycle for the offences punishable u/s 337, 338 of IPC.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW1.
PW1 denied that the injury sustained by him due to fall from foot path.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.

This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle which belongs to the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

14. ISSUE NO.2:
AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME: PW.1 has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.18.
As per this document, the petitioner was born on 23.03.1993.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was aged about 30 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '17'.
15.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to accident, he was working as an driver at CMM Hindustan Gold and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the same, he has produced Ex.P.16 - letter issued by CMM Hindustan SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.2735/2023 Gold.
But petitioner has not examined any authorized person of Ex.P.16.
Therefore, it is necessary to take notional income of the petitioner while calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.16,000/- as the accident took place in the year 2023.

As per guidelines, the total physical disability is assessed in 1/3rd of the whole body.
In this case the PW4 has assessed the disability of petitioner is physical disability at 51% and whole body is 17%.

19. It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.2735/2023 petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.4 to show his disability, but the documents placed on record shows that he has the physical disability at 17% to the whole body.
But by looking into the record it seems that PW.4 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 12% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.

21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings to some extent.
As per Ex.P.8 wound certificate he sustained fracture of both bones of right leg and doctor opined as said injury is grievous.
Thus, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.2735/2023 head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.48,000/- (16,000/- x 3) under this head.
23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :

As per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.12 for nearly 8 days and as per case sheet marked at Ex.P.25 (page No.17 - discharge summary) for 7 days, in total he took treatment as an inpatient for 15 days.
PW.4 has produced outpatient record to show that petitioner took follow-up treatment.

Therefore,
this tribunal inclines to award Rs.22,500/- under this head.

24. MEDICAL EXPENSES (including purchase of artificial limb):- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.15 - SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.2735/2023 bill receipt amounting to Rs.1,37,736/- and medical prescription receipt at Ex.P.14.
Though Insurance Company disputed the medical expenses, nothing has been elicited during cross examination.
The medical bills appear to be genuine.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .1,37,736/- rounded off to Rs.1,37,750/- towards Medical Expenses.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence, a sum of Rs.3,91,680/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 17 X 12/100) is awarded under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.2735/2023 normal pleasures and joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
PW.4 has stated that, petitioner need another surgery for removal of the implant and its estimated cost of surgery around Rs.60,000/-.
Hence, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
